--- LITERATURE CONFIRMING THE RESISTANCE PATHWAYS OF THE ZONE 2 ---
The transcription factor Coro is an important regulator of synaptic plasticity and memory formation. In the hippocampus, Coro modulates the structural and functional synaptice plasticities through the regulation of presynaptic release probability, synaptogenesis, and dendrite morphogenesis (Chen et al., 2012). The decrease in Coro expression may result in a decrease in the structrual and functional connectivity of the neurons and thus contributes to the loss of network activity.
The decrease in Cnr transcription may suggest a change in the morphology of neuronal structure, such as a decrease of neurite. The decrease of Htr transcription suggests a change of excitability of neuron, and the decrease of Rellan suggests a decreaseof network activity as well.
All of these changes together contribute to the resistance to the seizure induction.
CONCLUSION: Zone 2 represents a class of neurONs whose morphological and functional characteristics are consistent with their resistance to seizures. They have fewer connections and are less likely to generate strong responses.
